chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Washa', from Hammad ibn Uthman, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Whoever claims that God commands with immorality has lied against God, and whoever claims that good and evil are His (responsibility) has lied against God.

key_terms.الْخَيْرُ وَالشَّرُّ: Good and evil — the theological question of their ultimate authorship and causation
key_terms.الْفَحْشَاءُ: Immorality, indecency, obscenity — actions God explicitly forbids in the Quran (7:28, 16:90)
key_terms.زَعَمَ: To claim, allege — used for unfounded or false assertions
key_terms.كَذَبَ عَلَى اللَّهِ: To lie against God — the gravest form of falsehood in Islamic theology

ai.seo_question: Does God command immorality? What is the Shia view on divine predetermination and free will?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) issues a double refutation of two theological errors: the claim that God commands evil, and the claim that God is the author and cause of both good and evil actions in humans. This hadith is part of Chapter 30 of al-Kafi dealing with the theological position between absolute predetermination (jabr) and complete human autonomy (tafwid), affirming the Shia doctrine of 'the matter between two matters' (al-amr bayna al-amrayn). The original audience — Shia Muslims debating Ash'ari and Mu'tazilite positions — would have understood this as a rejection of both Jabrite fatalism (which can be read as attributing evil command to God) and certain Mu'tazilite positions on divine authorship of good and evil.

en.hubeali:
Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moalla Bin Muhammad, from Al Hassan Bin Ali Al Washa, from Hammad Bin Usman, from Abu Baseer, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘The one who claim that Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Commands with the immoralities, so he has lied upon Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, and the one who claims that the good and the evil are to Him<sup>azwj</sup> (His<sup>azwj</sup> Responsibility), so he has lied upon Allah<sup>azwj</sup>’.
